problem: Curiosity-driven RL in photorealistic 3D scenes collapses: agents get stuck in local loops and receive fresh intrinsic reward for revisiting forgotten states, because the learned world model is not persistent within an episode and the policy lacks episodic context.
motivation: Exploration is a prerequisite for sparse-reward long-horizon tasks like object retrieval or image-goal navigation. Existing map-based RL explorers (ANS, OccAnt) depend on explicit geometric maps and often depth, which limits transfer to semantic tasks. The paper argues that curiosity needs both a persistent, continuously updated world model and an agent with episodic memory.
key_idea: Compute a binary curiosity reward from an online 3DGS reconstruction that persists over the episode (training only), and train a long-context RGB-sequence transformer policy with PPO so it needs only RGB at test time.
insight: Both persistence and memory matter. Capping the 3DGS to the last 64 frames drops HM3D completeness@1024 from 74.94 to 38.09, and ICM variants collapse to 37-43. Shrinking the agent context (ctx=1: 50.39, RNN: 67.33) also degrades exploration. Even a critic-only memory beats no memory. Occasional uniform-random action injection helps the policy backtrack through reward-less stretches, and the end-to-end RGB policy fine-tunes better than from-scratch training on sparse-reward tasks.
method: Persistent 3DGS forward model: an online 3DGS is built from privileged RGB-D and pose, adding one Gaussian per pixel each step. It is optimized on 10 random past views every 16 steps and densified with 3DGS-MCMC. It renders the next pose before the observation is incorporated. Used only at training.

Curiosity reward: prediction error between the blurred, 4x-downsampled render and the observed frame is thresholded into a binary reward (r_new=0.5 if the error exceeds the threshold, r_old=2e-4 otherwise).
Agent encoder: each RGB frame is concatenated with a Plücker-ray image of the intended action. A learnable query cross-attends to the patch tokens and DINOv2 features to give one token per frame.

Long-context sequence model: sliding-window causal temporal self-attention, interleaved with a global linear-attention (TTT/LoGeR-style) memory module with a running state. Actor and critic heads sit on top. The policy uses only RGB and actions at test time.

PPO with random-action mixing: the behavior policy is (1-ε)π + ε·Uniform, with ε annealed from 0.2 to 0 over 5M steps starting at step 25M. The PPO ratio uses the behavior probability in the denominator, plus a small entropy bonus.

Drone embodiment: a free-flying sphere at 1.25 m with a 90° FOV camera. Actions are forward 0.25 m, turn ±15°, and pause. Collisions are ray-traced against the mesh, avoiding navmesh sliding shortcuts.
Downstream fine-tuning: the same architecture is fine-tuned with task reward for 8M steps. For image-goal navigation, the goal image token is attended densely by the temporal module.

setting.backbone: Custom transformer (sliding-window causal attention + linear-attention memory) with DINOv2 features, trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: HM3D train (800 scenes), curiosity reward only, 110M steps (5.5 days on 8xH100); no extra or web data. Fine-tuning uses 8M steps of task reward.
setting.observation: Monocular forward RGB stream (plus previous actions); RGB-D and pose are used only at training for the reward
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: move forward 0.25 m, look left/right 15°, pause (free 3D drone, 1024-step episodes)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D, Gibson; World Labs AI-generated 3DGS worlds for OOD)
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth and pose are used only in training for the 3DGS reward); completeness evaluation uses GT meshes and depth

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3D val: 100 scenes x 2 random starts = 200 episodes, 1024 steps
numbers.backbone: Transformer+linear-attn memory policy, RGB only at test
numbers.extra: Trained with curiosity only on HM3D train; the baselines ANS/OccAnt were retrained on the same data
numbers.evidence: Fig. 'comparison' table, HM3D columns, Ours row

numbers.eval_set_note: 86 Gibson scenes, 1 start each; zero-shot from HM3D
numbers.backbone: Transformer+linear-attn memory policy, RGB only at test
numbers.extra: Trained on HM3D only, not fine-tuned on Gibson
numbers.evidence: Fig. 'comparison' table, Gibson columns, Ours row

numbers_note: Apple-picking and image-goal success rates appear only in figures, with no numbers in the text. There are no standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks. Coverage benchmark names are custom.
results: On HM3D the method reaches 74.94% completeness@1024 (0.14 m avg dist), versus 74.62% (0.18) for OccAnt-RGBD, which uses GT depth, and 65-69% for RGB-only baselines. It generalizes zero-shot to Gibson (82.42% vs 81.23% for OccAnt-RGBD). Fine-tuned agents beat from-scratch on apple picking and image-goal navigation, and the policy explores AI-generated worlds with only 2-3 collisions over 256 steps.
limitations: Static scenes only, since 3DGS is the persistent world model. The reward also requires depth and pose at training time.
Trained and evaluated on a free-flying drone with deterministic motion, not a ground robot with noise. No real-robot experiments.
Downstream and OOD results are mostly qualitative or in figures. Training is expensive (110M steps, 8xH100 for 5.5 days).
